overview: This single-page Department of State filing aid lists papers concerning Japanese navigation laws, maritime safety, coastal trade, travel restrictions, and port traffic. Its entries refer to a Japanese vessel-safety law, restrictions on foreign participation in the Dairen–Korea coasting trade, Japanese obstruction of American President Lines vessels at the Nantao boom in Shanghai, a temporary prohibition on foreigners traveling through the Seto Inland Sea, and requested statistics on merchant ships entering and leaving Vladivostok. Several entries are cross-references to documents filed elsewhere in the State Department decimal file.

subfiles.title: List of papers on Japanese navigation laws and regulations
subfiles.about: A departmental index summarizes and cross-references papers concerning Japanese maritime law, coastal trade, navigation restrictions, and merchant-shipping movements.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records a Kobe report enclosing a new Japanese vessel-safety law, said to have entered operation on March 1, 1934, although the entry gives a later passage date of March 14, 1935. Other entries concern foreign participation in the Dairen–Korea coasting trade, a Texas Company protest, and Japanese restrictions affecting President Lines vessels at Shanghai's Nantao boom. It also points to reports about foreigners and American missionaries being barred from Seto Inland Sea travel during February 15–25 and about merchant ships entering and clearing Vladivostok, including their flags, arrival and departure dates, previous ports, and destinations.

interest: The sheet is useful as a compact map of maritime disputes and controls involving Japan and American interests during the 1930s, even though most of the substantive documents were filed under other decimal classifications. It connects formal safety legislation with discriminatory coastal-trade rules, restrictions on missionary travel, interference with American shipping at Shanghai, and intelligence gathering on Soviet Far Eastern port traffic. It is also valuable for reconstructing dispersed archival documentation through its file references, telegram numbers, officials' names, and brief descriptions of otherwise absent papers.
